result.title: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement
result.summary: Robots are increasingly autonomous in task execution, yet their improvement remains largely human-driven. This study investigates Physical Recursive Self-Improvement (Physical RSI), in which physical experience guides lasting updates to both a robot's capabilities and its improvement procedure, making subsequent improvement more effective across tasks. Physical RSI faces challenges from noisy observations, continuous dynamics, costly trials, and irreversible consequences. We present an L0-L5 framework that differentiates capability-level from meta-level updates and within-task from across-task gains, reserving L5 for independently verified recursive gain. We study existing methods around harness adaptation and model training, alongside safety and control mechanisms that govern execution and successive updates. Our analysis reveals that, despite substantial progress in self-improvement, the surveyed literature does not yet demonstrate Physical RSI as defined by our framework. We identify research priorities in reliable feedback, causal attribution, safety preservation, and benchmarking, outlining a path toward robots that autonomously improve how they learn while ensuring safety. The GitHub repository for Physical RSI is available at https://github.com/SAIL-Research-Lab/Physical-RSI.

AI.brief_summary: 这是一篇关于「物理递归自我改进」（Physical RSI）的综述：作者提出 L0–L5 框架，区分能力层与元层更新、任务内与跨任务收益，并以此审视现有机器人自我改进方法，指出当前文献尚未展示符合其定义的物理 RSI。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属机器人领域，但其中「元层更新改进过程本身」的划分以及对可靠反馈与因果归因的强调，可能与 LVR 中推理过程/轨迹训练的自我改进与贡献分配问题形成概念参照，具体可迁移性需核查。
